prerequisites: It is recommended that the student possesses the knowledge acquired in the subjects of Mathematics I and Mathematics II: differential and integral calculus, linear algebra, as well as the numerical methods characteristic of these topics.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge on: linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; differential and partial differential equations; numerical methods; numerical algorithms; statistics and optimization.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Teamwork. Actively collaborate with a group of people to achieve a common goal by combining different talents.

Has the aptitude to apply the acquired knowledge on the following topics of Differential and Partial Differential Equations: First-order ordinary differential equations; higher-order linear equations; linear systems; Laplace Transform; Fourier series; partial differential equations; application to mathematical physics equations; Runge-Kutta methods for IVP and finite difference methods for boundary value problems.
Solves mathematical problems that may arise in Engineering.
Knows how to use numerical methods and mathematical software in solving some mathematical problems.
Has the skill to handle mathematical language; in particular, symbolic and formal language.
Knows the reflective use of symbolic and numerical calculation tools.
Possesses skills characteristic of scientific-mathematical thinking, which allow them to ask and answer mathematical questions, correctly and rigorously.

syllabus_topics: First-order equations: Existence and uniqueness of solutions. Elementary integration methods. Applications.
Higher-order linear equations: Equations with constant coefficients. Cauchy-Euler equation. Applications.
Linear systems: First-order systems with constant coefficients. Applications.
Fourier series. Separation of variables method. Numerical resolution of boundary value problems.
teaching_methods: Lectures (presenting theoretical content along with examples and practical questions, complemented with problem classes)
Problem solving sessions (providing a collection of problems, some solved in class, others for recommended self-study)
Computer practicals (6 sessions of 2 hours analyzing and programming mathematical algorithms using symbolic and numerical programming software)

assessment_methods.method: Test on theoretical-practical contents of the subject
Test on topics developed in practical sessions

assessment_rules: The final grade F is obtained by F = E + L if E is not less than 3.2 (out of 8), otherwise F = E. E is the score from the theoretical-practical exam (80% weight), and L is the score from the practical sessions test (20% weight). Voluntary tests may be offered during the semester to facilitate gradual progression. The second call will be evaluated by a global test with the same characteristics as the first call. The transversal competence (UZ1) teamwork will be evaluated through activities proposed by the faculty during some practical sessions.
